result.be:
All three backend fixes are in, and the full workspace test suite and the release build both pass. I edited only `crates/`, made no commits, and removed all my test folders. After calibration, the time estimate lands within 2–8% of the actual time for both modes.

**1. Space freed now matches what was actually deleted** (`execute.rs`)
- The expected amount for each source drive counts direct deletes, files the Recycle Bin refused (Windows deleted those outright) and cross-drive quarantine. Recycle Bin and same-drive quarantine count as nothing freed.
- `freed_bytes` is 0 when nothing was expected to be freed. Otherwise it is the measured change in free space, kept between 0 and expected × 1.1 + 64 MB.
- The raw measured change is kept in the report as `freed_measured_bytes`. I also added `freed_expected_bytes`. Both go into the summary log line.
- This fixes the "D 盘多出 0.18 GB" shown next to "直接删除 0 B": that case now reports 0.

**2. Time estimate and progress bar cover the finishing work** (`execute.rs`, `perf.rs`, `preflight.rs`)
- The estimate and the bar's total now include removing emptied folders and writing the quarantine manifest. Both happen on a single thread, so the estimate no longer divides them across threads.
- The bar advances for each folder checked and once after the manifest is written, so it no longer sits near 100% during that work. It now hits exactly 100% at the end of a run that wasn't stopped.
- New defaults: `permanent_ms` 0.15 (was 0.20), `rmdir_ms` 0.25 (was 0.1), new `manifest_ms` 0.002. Folder and manifest costs are learned from what is measured, and the per-file learning no longer absorbs the finishing time. EMA α is now 0.5 instead of 0.3.
- An existing `perf.json` without `manifest_ms` still loads, with `rmdir_ms` reset to the new default.

Calibration ran through the bench test on D:, 100k files of 64 bytes each:

| Mode | Folders | Estimate | Actual | Actual / estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Permanent delete | 2,100 | 5.2 s | 4.88 s | 0.94 |
| Same-drive quarantine | 2,100 | 20.2 s | 18.68 s | 0.92 |
| Permanent delete | 20,500 | 9.8 s | 9.36 s | 0.96 |
| Same-drive quarantine | 20,500 | 24.8 s | 24.43 s | 0.98 |

- **Bar pacing:** for example, 50% at 4.9 s of a 9.4 s run, and with 20,500 folders the bar keeps moving through the last 4.7 s of folder removal. The remaining time, worked out the same way the UI does it, stayed within about ±2 s of the true remaining time.
- **Before the change:** the old code estimated 6.2 s for permanent delete and took 4.56 s (0.74, outside ±25%).
- **Learning:** starting from deliberately wrong values, four runs moved them steadily toward the measured ones.

Measured folder removal costs about 0.25 ms per folder. On a cache with many folders, that single-threaded tail is now counted, but it is not faster.

**3. Tiny files no longer counted as a full 4 KB block** (`fs.rs`, `scan.rs`, `win.rs`, `model.rs`, `plan.rs`, `preflight.rs`, `mod.rs`)
- **Measured on D:** (NTFS, 4 KB blocks) by comparing two Windows size queries. The basic size query (`GetCompressedFileSizeW`) always returns the file's logical size, so it can't tell stored-in-the-file-table files apart. The real allocation (`FileStandardInfo.AllocationSize`) can:

| File name length | Stored in the file table (no blocks used) | Gets a full 4 KB block |
|---|---|---|
| 6 characters | up to 720 bytes (allocation 720) | from 750 bytes (allocation 4096) |
| 115 characters | up to 500 bytes (allocation 504) | from 600 bytes (allocation 4096) |

- **Docs:** this matches Microsoft's ["The Four Stages of NTFS File Growth"](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/askcore/the-four-stages-of-ntfs-file-growth) and ["How NTFS Works"](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2003/cc781134(v=ws.10)), which put the limit at roughly 900 bytes.
- **One shared rule:** a new helper `fs::cluster_bytes` is used by the scan, by plan building and by preflight. It applies only on NTFS, and only to files that aren't compressed, sparse or links. If the real allocation is known and is smaller than one block, the file counts as 0.
- **The default scan mode now reads the real allocation** for small files. Fast mode and fallbacks can't, so they guess from file size and name length, leaning towards counting a full block.
- **Tests added:**
  - a unit test of the rule;
  - a real-disk test checking scan and preflight agree for 0, 64, 400, 700, 800, 1000 and 5000-byte files;
  - an update to the existing real-file-size test: a 1-byte file now counts as 0 on NTFS.

**4. Tests and build**
- `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1` with `DISKWHY_TEST_XVOL_DIR=D:\desk\claudex\13\dw-test-xvol-p`: exit 0. Results:
  - core unit tests 24
  - action tests 49 (115.98 s)
  - crash tests 4
  - duplicate-file tests 5, plus 1 ignored
  - explain tests 39
  - mock tests 8
  - real-disk tests 6
  - Tauri shell 1
  - bench 1 ignored
  - Total: 136 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored.
- The cross-drive quarantine test actually ran rather than being skipped.
- `cargo build --release -p diskwhy`: "Finished `release` profile … in 3m 56s".

**Not verified:**
- **Release app not run:** no UI run and no real C: data.
  - Calibration used the bench test, not the app. The earlier app run deleted about 2× slower per file (125k in 10.9 s) than the bench does (100k in 4.9 s). So the first estimate in the app may come out short until it learns from a run or two.
  - I didn't test with the log on C: as the app has it, because test files had to stay under `D:\desk\claudex\13\dw-test-*`.
- **No "before" run on the 20,500-folder data:** the old code's estimate there is calculated, not measured (about 6.7 s against roughly 9.3 s actual).
- **Fast mode's size guess** has no measured basis on drives with 4 KB file-table records or with 8.3 short names turned on.

**Files changed:**
- Source: `execute.rs`, `perf.rs`, `preflight.rs`, `plan.rs` and `mod.rs` in `crates/diskwhy-core/src/action/`, plus `fs.rs`, `scan.rs`, `win.rs` and `model.rs` in `crates/diskwhy-core/src/`.
- Tests: `action_tests.rs`, `bench_tests.rs`, `real_fs_tests.rs`, `dedup_tests.rs` and `mock_tests.rs` in `crates/diskwhy-core/tests/`. `bench_tests.rs` gained a progress timeline, folder-heavy test cases, and the `DISKWHY_BENCH_PERF` and `DISKWHY_BENCH_LOG_DIR` env vars. The other test files needed small updates for the new fields.

For the frontend lane: `freed_bytes` keeps its name and meaning (now the capped value), and the report gains `freed_measured_bytes` and `freed_expected_bytes`. `src-tauri/src` needed no changes.
